channel.title: ICU Scope
channel.description: Daily-updated ICU/critical-care literature and FOAMed, organized by organ system.

item.title: Causal mediation analysis of contact with COVID-19 patients and burnout syndrome in physiotherapists in Japan: secondary analysis of a multicentre observational study.
item.description: This study looked at Japanese physiotherapists who worked with COVID-19 patients and found that direct contact with patients contributed to burnout, but this effect was partly buffered by appreciation and respect from patients and colleagues. The study suggests that organisational resources, such as reimbursement for care, may also play a role in burnout. Burnout prevalence was 19.4% among the physiotherapists.

item.title: Mechanisms and therapeutic strategies of pyroptosis in sepsis‑induced acute lung injury (Review).
item.description: This review explores the mechanisms and therapeutic strategies of pyroptosis in sepsis-induced acute lung injury. Pyroptosis is a critical driver of lung injury and inflammation, and its pathways can be targeted for personalized treatments. Researchers have identified biomarkers and potential inhibitors to enable more effective interventions.

item.title: Fluid and Electrolyte Management in Critically Ill Patients with Infections.
item.description: Critically ill patients with infections struggle to maintain fluid balance due to increased capillary permeability and organ dysfunction. Inadequate fluid balance can increase complications, morbidity, and mortality. Skilled nursing and advanced monitoring are essential to optimize outcomes.

item.title: Limited Versus Extended Trophic Feeding (LET-FEED) Trial
item.description: This study compared two feeding regimens in preterm infants born between 25w0d and 31w6d. The regimens differed in when enteral feeds were advanced, either after 24 hours or after 72 hours. The study found no difference in the risk of late onset sepsis or other adverse outcomes between the two groups.

item.title: Epidemiology of Antimicrobial-use and Antimicrobial-resistant Infections in Four Hospitals in Thailand
item.description: This study aims to investigate the impact of antibiotic de-escalation on patients who received a short-course of parenteral antibiotics. The study will analyze past medical records from four public referral hospitals in Thailand to understand the effects of de-escalation on patients. The study will identify which types of patients are more likely to receive antibiotic de-escalation.

item.title: Platelets in Pregnancy
item.description: This study evaluated platelet changes in pregnant patients at high-risk for preeclampsia before and after aspirin use. Blood samples were collected to assess the association between platelet changes and adverse perinatal outcomes. No significant findings were reported.

item.title: Higher-Dose Dexamethasone Improves Breathing and Shortens NICU Stay in Preterm Babies
item.description: This observational study compared the effects of two doses of dexamethasone given to pregnant women at risk of preterm birth on preterm babies' breathing and NICU stay. The study found that higher-dose dexamethasone improved breathing and shortened NICU stay in preterm babies. The study looked at preterm babies born between 26 and 36 weeks of pregnancy.

item.title: The Family-ICU Trial
item.description: This study aimed to assess whether family participation in adult ICU rounds improves family satisfaction and patient outcomes. However, the study did not report any key numbers.

item.title: Development and Validation of an Ultrasound-Based Difficult Cannulation Risk Score for Pre-procedural Internal Jugular Vein Catheterization in Critically Ill Patients: A Prospective Observational Cohort Study
item.description: Researchers developed and validated a score to predict difficult cannulation during ultrasound-guided internal jugular vein catheterization in critically ill patients. The score considers pre-procedural characteristics of the IJV and its anatomical relationship with the common carotid artery. The study aimed to improve procedural success and reduce the risk of mechanical complications.

item.title: A Study on How the Immune System Responds to Sepsis and Its Long-term Effects
item.description: Sepsis occurs when an infection disrupts the body's immune balance, potentially leading to life-threatening damage or failure of healthy organs. Survivors may experience long-term health problems. The immune response can become either too strong or too weak.

item.title: A Trial of Staff Time With Proned Patients in the ICU Using the 'BathMat'
item.description: This study investigated the use of the 'BathMat' to assist with proning patients in the ICU, which involves lying patients on their front to improve oxygenation. The BathMat is a tool used to help reposition patients every 2-4 hours to prevent sores and injuries. The study aimed to assess the feasibility and effectiveness of using the BathMat in this context.

item.title: A Study to Evaluate AZD7760 Safety and Pharmacokinetics in Healthy Adults (Phase I) and Adults With End-stage Kidney Disease on Hemodialysis With a Central Venous Catheter (Phase IIa)
item.description: This study evaluated the safety and pharmacokinetics of AZD7760 in healthy adults and those with end-stage kidney disease on hemodialysis. Participants received AZD7760 as an intravenous infusion. The study aimed to assess the drug's safety and how it is absorbed and processed in the body.

item.title: Machine Learning Prediction of Mortality After Prone Positioning in ARDS
item.description: Researchers developed a machine learning model to predict mortality after prone positioning in patients with acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). The model was trained and validated on a large dataset of 1200 patients. The study aimed to improve clinical decision-making by identifying high-risk patients.

item.title: Comparison of NEWS2 and Machine Learning for Early Sepsis Warning
item.description: This study compared the early warning performance of a NEWS2-based clinical decision support system (KDS) to a machine learning model in predicting sepsis diagnosis. The NEWS2-based KDS provided an alert 4.5 hours before sepsis diagnosis, on average. The machine learning model was externally validated on 2000 patients.

item.title: HYDROcortisone Versus Placebo for Severe HospItal-acquired Pneumonia in Intensive Care Patients: the HYDRO-SHIP Study
item.description: The HYDRO-SHIP study was a multicenter randomized trial investigating the use of hydrocortisone plus standard therapy in critical care patients with hospital-acquired pneumonia. This is the first study to explore the use of corticosteroids in this type of infection. The study aims to improve the outcome of patients with nosocomial pneumonia.

item.title: The Case of the Redacted Ledger
item.description: This commentary discusses the lack of randomized controlled trials examining the efficacy of oseltamivir, citing past instances of Roche hiding borderline efficacy results for profit.

item.title: Physiological Changes in Adult Intensive Care Patients Following Contact With Their Primary Caregiver
item.description: This study examined the effect of physical contact with primary caregivers on adult ICU patients' physiological responses. The trial was a randomized controlled study. No significant physiological changes were found.

item.title: Call for Life Sepsis
item.description: Sepsis is a life-threatening condition caused by a host response to infection, with high mortality rates in sub-Saharan Africa. Children under 5 years hospitalized with sepsis have high mortality rates within the first 6 months of discharge. Various populations in sub-Saharan Africa experience high mortality rates due to sepsis.

item.title: ICU Delirium Playbook Training Study for ICU Nurses
item.description: A study was conducted to evaluate the effectiveness of a delirium playbook training for ICU nurses. The training aimed to improve delirium recognition and management. However, no specific results were reported.

item.title: Transpulmonary Pressure-guided Mechanical Ventilation Strategy in Right Ventricular Protection in Patients With ARDS
item.description: Researchers investigated whether a specific mechanical ventilation strategy, guided by transpulmonary pressure, can reduce right ventricular involvement in patients with moderate to severe ARDS caused by pneumonia.

item.title: CT-Determined Sarcopenia and Mortality in Critically Ill Cancer Patients
item.description: This observational study evaluated the relationship between sarcopenia and muscle quality impairment in critically ill cancer patients and their risk of 28-day mortality. The study used computed tomography to assess muscle quality and found an association between lower muscle quality and increased mortality. The study aimed to answer whether lower psoas muscle quality is associated with increased mortality in critically ill cancer patients.

item.title: Impact of Direct Antimicrobial Susceptibility Testing on Respiratory Sample of Intensive Care Patient With Suspected VAP
item.description: The study discusses the impact of direct antimicrobial susceptibility testing on respiratory samples of ICU patients with suspected ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP). Current guidelines recommend using broad-spectrum antibiotics, but this may promote antibiotic resistance. The study aims to explore the benefits of direct AST in reducing inappropriate antibiotic therapy.

item.title: Preventive Narrative Exposure Intervention for PTSD in ICU Patients After Cardiopulmonary Bypass Cardiac Surgery
item.description: This study evaluates an ICU-based intervention to prevent posttraumatic stress symptoms in adult patients after cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass. Participants were randomly assigned to either an intervention group or a control group. The study aims to determine if the intervention is effective in preventing posttraumatic stress symptoms.

item.title: Exploring the Effectiveness of an Application Intervention on Cognitive, Learning Self-Efficacy,and Clinical Reasoning of Nurses Regarding Delirium Education in the Intensive Care Unit
item.description: This study evaluated the effectiveness of an app-based delirium education program for ICU nurses. The program aimed to enhance nurses' knowledge, learning self-efficacy, and clinical reasoning regarding delirium. The study found that the app intervention had a positive impact on nurses' knowledge and learning self-efficacy.

item.title: Hemoglobin Trends as a Predictor of Outcomes in Critically Ill Patients (The TRENT-ICU Study)
item.description: This observational study examined if early hemoglobin decline in critically ill patients can predict longer ICU stays and in-hospital mortality. The study found that early hemoglobin decline is associated with these outcomes. The study aims to answer two main questions about the relationship between hemoglobin decline and patient outcomes.

item.title: What place for pragmatic RCTs in intensive care?
item.description: This article discusses the limitations of pragmatic randomized controlled trials (RCTs) in intensive care units (ICUs). Pragmatic RCTs often fail to demonstrate outcome differences due to heterogeneity of ICU populations and suboptimal trial performance. Suggestions for improvement are provided.

item.title: Net Ultrafiltration Rate and Mortality in Critically Ill Patients: A Multicenter Cohort Study With Analysis of Fluid Balance Changes.
item.description: This study investigated the relationship between net ultrafiltration rate and fluid balance changes in critically ill patients receiving continuous renal replacement therapy. The results showed that fluid balance change, not net ultrafiltration rate, was the key determinant of outcome. The study found that more positive fluid balance changes were linked to adverse clinical outcomes.

item.title: What place for pragmatic RCTs in intensive care?
item.description: This article discusses the limitations of pragmatic randomized controlled trials (RCTs) in intensive care units (ICUs). Pragmatic RCTs often fail to demonstrate outcome differences due to heterogeneity of ICU populations and suboptimal trial performance. Suggestions for improvement are provided.

item.title: Assessment of Reintubation Risk Using Multiple Parameters in Postoperative Intensive Care Unit Patients
item.description: This study evaluates the risk of reintubation in postoperative ICU patients using multiple parameters. The study aims to identify factors associated with reintubation after extubation. The study will include adult patients who are extubated in the operating room and admitted to the ICU.

item.title: Candida PCR Diagnosis Strategy in Patients From Intensive Care Units
item.description: Researchers evaluated a new PCR technique for diagnosing invasive candidiasis in ICU patients. The goal was to see if this method could provide faster results, allowing for earlier antifungal treatment. This could help prevent resistance and reduce healthcare costs.

item.title: Enhanced Mentor Mother Strategy for Pregnant and Postpartum Women Living With HIV
item.description: This study will test an enhanced mentor mother strategy that uses differentiated service delivery to support pregnant and postpartum women living with HIV in resource-limited settings.

item.title: Impact of Procalcitonin-guided Algorithm on Early Discontinuation of Antibiotic Therapy
item.description: This study tested a procalcitonin-guided algorithm to discontinue antibiotic treatment in critically ill children. Patients were randomly assigned to either a PCT-guided group or a standard-of-care group. The study found that the PCT-guided algorithm was used to discontinue antibiotic treatment.

item.title: COMPARE-VENT Feasibility Pilot Study
item.description: The COMPARE-VENT Feasibility Pilot Study explored the challenges of cardiac intensive care unit (CICU) admissions, particularly those requiring advanced respiratory support and invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV). These patients often have impaired cardiovascular reserve, making them vulnerable to the adverse effects of positive pressure ventilation (PPV) and systemic sedation. The study aimed to assess the feasibility of a new approach to address these challenges.

item.title: A Prospective Observational Study Using the FAM-CAM
item.description: This study observed whether family members can identify signs of delirium in ICU patients that may not be detected by routine screening. Participants received usual medical care. Family members were asked to report any signs of delirium.

item.title: Resuscitative TEE Collaborative Registry
item.description: This study evaluated the clinical impact and safety of focused, point-of-care transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) in critically-ill patients. The study aimed to determine the clinical impact and safety of TEE performed during routine clinical care. No specific findings were reported.

item.title: Diffuse Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS), Recruitment Maneuver, and sRAGE (DAMAGE Study)
item.description: This study investigated the effect of a recruitment maneuver on plasma sRAGE levels in patients with ALI/ARDS. The study found that a recruitment maneuver increased plasma sRAGE levels. The study was a prospective monocentric randomized controlled cross-over study.

item.title: Impact of Metabolite Supplementation to Restore Mitochondrial Dysfunction During Septic Shock: a Preclinical Study
item.description: This preclinical study investigated the impact of exogenous metabolites on restoring mitochondrial function in septic shock patients with lactate acidosis. The study aimed to evaluate the effect of metabolite supplementation on mitochondrial metabolism in septic shock. The results of this study are not reported.

item.title: Fluid Administration and Fluid Accumulation in the Intensive Care Unit
item.description: This study aimed to describe fluid administration and accumulation in ICU patients. It provided contemporary data on fluid accumulation, risk factors, management, and outcomes in critically ill adults. The study did not report any specific findings or results.

item.title: Clinical Performance of 3D-Printed vs. Milled Endocrowns
item.description: This clinical trial compared the durability and functionality of 3D-printed versus milled endocrowns in the oral cavity. The study aimed to investigate the effect of different materials on clinical success. No results were reported.

item.title: Vadadustat for the Treatment of Nonintubated Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome Due to Pathogen-Associated Lung Injury
item.description: This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of vadadustat in treating nonintubated patients with ARDS caused by pathogen-associated lung injury. No results were reported.

item.title: Heterogeneous Treatment Effects of Renal Replacement Therapy in Critically Ill Patients: A Multicenter Observational Study Using a Japanese ICU Registry.
item.description: This study used a large Japanese ICU registry to investigate the effects of renal replacement therapy (RRT) on hospital mortality. While RRT was associated with higher hospital mortality overall, the study found that certain subgroups of patients may benefit from RRT, such as those with elevated serum creatinine, reduced urine output, and elevated blood urea nitrogen levels.

item.title: The impact of an intensive care telemedicine program on weaning from invasive ventilation: a secondary analysis of the ERIC trial.
item.description: BACKGROUND: ICU patients commonly require invasive mechanical ventilation. Although weaning from ventilation is crucial for patient outcomes, it is commonly not performed according to guideline recommendations. We investigated if a complex telemedicine intervention improves the weaning process and outcomes. item.title: EMCrit 431 – OB-EMCrit – Life-Threatening Post-Partum Hemorrhage (PPH) with Cho Espinoza
item.description: Dr. Cho Espinosa discusses how to manage life-threatening post-partum hemorrhage with a focus on uterotonic administration, physical compression techniques, and coagulopathy management.

item.title: A Slow Retreat
item.description: The standard of care for post-cardiac arrest management, targeted temperature management (TTM), may be based on a flawed premise. The evidence supporting TTM has been questioned. The foundation of TTM is being reevaluated.

item.title: Diaphragmatic Ultrasonography in Difficult Weaning
item.description: Researchers used ultrasound to assess diaphragmatic and extradiaphragmatic muscles in patients with difficult weaning from mechanical ventilation. They found that diaphragmatic ultrasonography can help determine the readiness of patients for weaning. The study suggests that this method may improve the success rate of weaning.

item.title: Soluble Forms and Ligands of RAGE in ALI/ARDS (SoLiRAGE).
item.description: Researchers studied soluble forms and ligands of RAGE in patients with Acute Lung Injury (ALI) and Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS). They found elevated levels of soluble RAGE in plasma and pulmonary edema fluid from these patients. This may be a novel marker of alveolar epithelial type I cell injury.

item.title: Pulmonary and Ventilatory Effects of Bed Verticalization in Patients With Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome
item.description: This study investigated the effects of bed verticalization on patients with acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). The study found no reported pulmonary and ventilatory effects of bed verticalization in patients with ARDS. No specific outcomes were reported.

item.title: Blood Culture Collection Strategies for Suspected Bloodstream Infection
item.description: This study compares two blood culture collection strategies in adults with suspected sepsis. The goal is to evaluate their diagnostic performance and potential impact on patient discomfort and contamination risk.

item.title: Early Sepsis Recognition Tool
item.description: Researchers developed an early recognition tool for sepsis in children based on the Phoenix definition. They also investigated how to implement this tool in clinical practice. The study aimed to address the need for evidence-based approaches to identifying sepsis in diverse healthcare settings in Asia.

item.title: Conservative Oxygen for Unresponsive Patients after Cardiac Arrest.
item.description: BACKGROUND: In patients who are unresponsive after resuscitation from cardiac arrest, limiting oxygen exposure to that necessary to achieve acceptable oxygenation may increase the likelihood of survival with a favorable functional outcome. METHODS: We randomly assigned unresponsive adults receiving mechanical ventilation in the intensive care unit (ICU) after cardiac arrest to conservative or liberal oxygen therapy. item.title: GRAM NEGATIVES STUDY
item.description: This study aimed to develop a predictive model for mortality in critically ill patients with multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria. It also investigated the characteristics of patients who acquire colonization during ICU stay and the infectious complications they develop.

item.title: STimulation to Activate RespIration
item.description: This was a feasibility trial to test the safety and practicality of using diaphragm neurostimulation-assisted ventilation in patients on mechanical ventilation for acute hypoxemic respiratory failure with lung injury.

item.title: Cardiovascular Protection After Preeclampsia With Enalapril
item.description: This study aimed to assess the willingness of postpartum women to be randomized to different blood pressure medications and their effect on blood pressure in women with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy. However, it did not find any participants willing to be randomized.

item.title: RESTORE-ZG: Return of Effective Spontaneous Circulation Resuscitation Evaluation Canton of Zug
item.description: This study evaluated cardiac arrest care provided by emergency medical services in Switzerland, focusing on factors that influence return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC). The study aimed to identify predictors of ROSC in out-of-hospital cardiac arrests. No specific outcomes or effect measures were reported.

item.title: PulmCrit Wee: Four reasons that hyperangulated videolaryngoscopy should be the mainstay of ICU intubations
item.description: The author advocates for hyperangulated videolaryngoscopy as the primary method for intubating critically ill patients, citing several reasons for this recommendation.

item.title: İntensive Care Sepsis Prevelance in Turkey (INSEP-TURK)
item.description: This study aimed to determine the prevalence of sepsis and septic shock in adult intensive care units in Turkey. However, it appears to be a descriptive study without explicit findings on prevalence or other key statistics.
